metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.accountability_wording: the resulting contribution is the responsibility of the human contributor

evidence.quote: As with any tool, the resulting contribution is the responsibility of the human contributor.
Using AI output without ensuring that you fully understand the output or without verifying that it is the correct approach.
Translating or proof-reading your comments or PR descriptions. Please keep the wording as close as possible to your original wording.

domains.reasoning: The Generative AI section explicitly frames acceptable/unacceptable AI uses for PRs, issues and comments (code_contributions domain), requiring the human to understand/verify AI output before use (human_in_the_loop) and stating the contributor bears responsibility for the resulting contribution. Both supervision level and accountability holder are present.

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level stated for meeting recording/notetaker bots; no accountability holder named
domains.reasoning: The file discusses the new contributors meeting and meeting notes but never mentions AI notetakers, recording bots, or transcription tools.

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level for AI use in documentation/blog/design contributions; no accountability holder named
domains.reasoning: The Documentation section (typo fixes, docstrings, tutorials) does not mention AI at all, and the separate 'Use of Generative AI' section only names PRs, issues and GitHub/Discourse comments, not documentation or other content artifacts.

evidence.quote: To ensure project health and preserve limited core developer capacity, we will flag and reject low-value contributions that we believe are AI generated.

domains.rationale_only_mention: To ensure project health and preserve limited core developer capacity, we will flag and reject low-value contributions that we believe are AI generated. We may ban and/or report users to GitHub if they harm the project or its community through irresponsible use of AI.
domains.suggested_improvement: no stated rule on AI's role in moderation itself; no accountability holder named
domains.reasoning: The flagging/rejecting/banning language is enforcement machinery for the code_contributions AI rule, justified by preserving 'limited core developer capacity' (maintainer time/moderation load), not a rule about how AI may be used in moderation actions themselves. This is rationale, not provision, for the moderation domain.

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level for AI-assisted review; no accountability holder named
domains.reasoning: The document discusses human review processes (submitting reviews, PR review comments, pre-reviews in the incubator) but never states whether or how AI tools may be used by a reviewer.

domains.accountability_wording: the resulting contribution is the responsibility of the human contributor

evidence.quote: External AI tooling (e.g. bots, agents) directly interacting with the project; including creating issues, PRs or commenting on GitHub or Discourse.
As with any tool, the resulting contribution is the responsibility of the human contributor.

domains.reasoning: Agentic/bot interaction with the repository (creating issues, PRs, or comments autonomously) is explicitly listed as an unacceptable use, i.e. banned, under the general framing that a human contributor bears responsibility for tool-assisted work.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of environmental impact as rule or rationale
domains.reasoning: No text in this file references energy, water, hardware, or carbon footprint concerns.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of server load or hardware/financing cost
domains.reasoning: The only capacity concern raised is 'limited core developer capacity', which is human/maintainer time (moderation), not machine or financial infrastructure strain.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on use of project data/content for model training
domains.reasoning: The file never discusses whether Matplotlib's issues, discussions, or other user-contributed data may be used to train AI models.

unscoped_statements.quote: As with any tool, the resulting contribution is the responsibility of the human contributor.
we will flag and reject low-value contributions that we believe are AI generated

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: The policy speaks specifically and restrictively about AI in code contributions and autonomous/agentic interaction (both tied to human contributor accountability and a ban on bots/agents acting directly on the repo), but is entirely silent on notetaker bots, documentation/content, AI-assisted review, moderation's own use of AI, environmental impact, infrastructure strain, and training data use of project content.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
